newsitem.title: USA: Ford doubles rebate on 1997 Taurus.
newsitem.headline: Ford doubles rebate on 1997 Taurus.

text.p: Ford Motor Co on Thursday confirmed that it has doubled the rebate it will pay to buyers of its 1997 Taurus, in what analysts called an effort to ensure the car keeps its coveted title of best-selling auto in America for another year.
A company spokeswoman said that as of December 13 the company will pay $1,000 to buyers of the 1997 Taurus. The incentive runs through April 2.
The spokeswoman said while Ford would like to hold the title again this year, the incentive was raised so that dealers would be competitive with other manufacturers.

"Now that the '96s are pretty well cleared out, the dealers are concentrating more on '97, and we wanted to make sure they were competitive with what other manufacturers are doing," said Joy Wolfe, a spokeswoman for Ford.

But analysts said the No. 2 automaker wanted to ensure it maintains its claim to having the best-selling auto in the United States. If the Taurus wins, it will be its fifth consecutive year at the top.
Through November, sales of the Taurus were nearly 10,000 ahead of its rival, the Honda Accord.
But sales of the redesigned Taurus, which was introduced a year ago, were off to a slower-than-expected start.
"It's my judgement that Ford is offering rebates to keep the sales crown," said Ron Glantz, an analyst for Dean Witter Reynolds.
Glantz pointed out that the $1,000 rebate is becoming an annual tradition for the Ford Taurus, and that some other manufacturers are offering even bigger rebates.
"It's also true that Ford wants to beat Honda Accord, and Honda is not offering rebates," Glantz said, adding that in September the company pushed dealers to sell the Taurus over other Ford models.
"You have not only incentives but you also have a lot of pressure on a retail system to move the Taurus," Glantz said.

Ford's Wolfe said the rebate will likely have more impact on the first quarter than on the current fourth quarter, as the plants have been closed since December 20 for the holidays and are therefore not building new cars.
She said the new rebate on the 1997 Taurus will actually cost the company less than the previous 1996 model incentive, which included the $1,000 rebate plus other carryover rebates.
"It's fully contained within our plan for our marketing for first quarter," Wolfe said.
